This PR does **not** close #787: Slices E/F remain, gated on F13.4 detection (#786). ## What Per design `doc/2026-11-01_design_id787.md` §6 row D: - **Corpus** (`doc/kitty-disambiguate-v1-fixtures.json`): 24 of the 40 cases gain a `browser` field — the browser key event for the same keystroke plus the exact bytes the Slice C rich encoder must emit (the encoder's canonical form where the fixture's terminal input is an alternate form, e.g. F1 tilde vs letter). - **Roc oracle** (`pkgs/id/scripts/key-parity-generate.py` + `key-parity-test.sh`): generates one `expect` per case into a scratch copy of `examples/roc-world/Key.roc` and runs the pinned `roc test` — terminal bytes and browser bytes both decode through the **actual compiled `Key.parse_events`**, never a re-implemented decoder. Comparison zeroes the per-event `source` (which byte form produced the event); parity = key + modifiers + kind, plus `EventUnknown` payloads. items.title: feat(id): kitty keyboard slices E+F — SSH negotiation/framing and browser opt-in (#787)
items.body: Implements the two remaining slices of #787 per `doc/2026-11-01_design_id787.md` §6. Slices A–D were already on main (Roc decoder #4438, assembler, browser encoder #7734, parity oracle #12926), and the F13.4 startup probe already records `kitty_keyboard` support in the SSH adapter — this PR wires activation to that evidence. **This PR does not close #787**: the issue's final acceptance also wants one supported-terminal smoke session (and the unsupported fallback) recorded against a real terminal, which a remote test run cannot supply. ## Slice E — opt-in SSH lifecycle integration (`world_ssh`) - New `SshServeOptions { kitty_keyboard }` (default off); `serve()` delegates to `serve_with_options()`. The serve command maps env `ID_WORLD_SSH_KITTY_KEYBOARD=1` to it, following the existing `ID_WORLD_*` env pattern, with a status line when enabled. - On a raw session (never command/explorer/exec), after the F13.4 probe closes with uncontradicted kitty support, the session writes the profile push `CSI > 1 u` + flags query `CSI ? u` and **verifies before admitting any key**: tokens assembled during verification are held; a flags report carrying the disambiguation bit activates framing, one without it — or a 500 ms timeout — pops the owned push and falls back to legacy chunk input with held bytes untouched. One attempt per connection (no renegotiation loop). - While active, input runs through the Slice B assembler: one complete key token per durable `Input` event, exact bytes preserved, split/CSI/UTF-8 safe. Verification replies are consumed by an outstanding-query-only filter — never journaled. Framing errors, incomplete token at EOF/deadline, and input-queue loss past the activation baseline are fatal to the session (no unsafe resync). - Teardown pops exactly the owned push on every exit path (normal, refused, error, cancellation) before the alternate screen is left. Form answers route through the same engaged stream so the assembler cannot desync around them. - The assembler module moves from the `id` facade into `id-worlds` (the adapter's crate); the facade re-exports it, so `id::input_framing` is unchanged. ## Slice F — browser opt-in (`web`) - `world.ts` selects `richTerminalBytesForKey` per connection when the page is opened with `?keyboard=kitty`; legacy stays the default. Paste, the manual input form, and Meta/Dead/Process exclusions are unchanged in both modes. ## Tests - `world_ssh::kitty` unit tests: flags-report grammar, outstanding-only consumption, verify flip/refusal, coalesced key order, fallback byte fidelity, split tokens. - `world_ssh` integration tests (real russh client + world event subscription): negotiate → verify → split CSI-u framed as one event, Escape vs Alt+x as distinct events, no reply bytes journaled, exactly one pop at teardown; verification-refused fallback (held key delivered, legacy resumes, no second push); no negotiation without the opt-in; no push when the terminal reports no support. - Web: new `world-keyboard-optin.test.ts` — DOM → WebSocket in both modes (legacy bare Escape `1b` vs kitty `CSI 27 u`, Ctrl+i vs Tab, Alt+x), paste + shortcut exclusions under the opt-in. ## Verification state (read this before merging) Remote dispatches were queued while runner surfaces were exhausted; all three were still `queued` (no surface) when this PR was opened. Handles (branch head `00520a8a3`): - Rust tests (`cargo test -p id-worlds --features ssh world_ssh` + `input_framing`): `fp_250be4a8258466cd46be42840fee197b` - Web tests + typecheck: `fp_b7b9a7f0f820ca7eb716a93e47b95c1a` - Clippy (`id-worlds`, `id-cli`, `id`, all targets/features): `fp_ac36488f6ba6798b5a8af6a3cba2b93e` The jobs are recorded in the fleet queue and run when a surface frees; results land under `fleet queue session result `. Local verification was rustfmt only (remote-builds-only rule). No new dependencies. ## Residuals named in the design - Queue-loss fatality is observed on the recv path against the activation baseline; a drop claimed by the send path's viewer notice in the same instant could in principle race it — the window is one loop iteration and the failure mode degrades to today's legacy notice behavior. - Disambiguation only, per the design: no event-type/all-keys/alternate-key flags, no keyup path. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added optional kitty keyboard support for browser sessions, enabled with `?keyboard=kitty`. Other sessions continue to use legacy keyboard input. * Added opt-in kitty keyboard negotiation for SSH sessions. When the terminal supports it, key input is assembled into complete key events; unsupported terminals continue using legacy input. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved handling of incomplete or unverified keyboard input, preserving buffered input when SSH sessions fall back to legacy behavior.

items.title: feat(id): bounded raw input token assembler (inert, #787 slice B)
items.body:
Slice B of the landed #787 design (`doc/2026-11-01_design_id787.md` §4.2 and §6 row B).

Part of #787. This is one of six slices and does not close the issue; C–F remain.

## What this adds

A new, **inert** Rust module `pkgs/id/src/input_framing.rs` (plus its registration in
`src/lib.rs`) that turns arbitrary transport chunks into complete logical key tokens:

- Retains an incomplete UTF-8 scalar, CSI or SS3 sequence across `push` calls and
  emits one token per complete key, independent of how the transport split the bytes.
  Plain text emits one token per Unicode scalar.
- Token bytes are never rewritten; what the assembler emits is exactly what the
  transport received, so the durable `Input(Vec<u8>)` boundary is untouched.
- Bounds: 256-byte cap per pending token and a 5-second incomplete-token deadline
  (§4.2 safety defaults). Overlong tokens, invalid UTF-8, incomplete tokens at
  EOF/deadline and queue loss are fatal; the caller must close the session, because
  a missing prefix cannot be resynchronised.
- Connection-local state: one `InputAssembler` per raw connection, so interleaved
  connections cannot mix partial tokens.
- `ReplyFilter` seam only: `push_filtered` drops recognized control replies while
  preserving key order, for F13.4's demultiplexer to implement in slice E. No filter
  is provided that swallows unrecognized keys.

**No activation.** `world_ssh` does not call the module, the durable `Input` event,
journal format, guest ABI, browser encoder and lease/negotiation paths are unchanged.

## Tests

```
cd pkgs/id && cargo test --lib input_framing::tests
# 16 passed; 0 failed
```

Coverage follows the §6 done check: every split point and byte boundary of the fixture
corpus, coalesced keys, split probe-reply + key order, cap boundary (exactly 256 passes,
257 fails), unterminated over-cap, deadline, EOF with/without pending bytes, invalid
UTF-8 and overlong forms, malformed escapes, queue loss and interleaved connections.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. Default-feature targeted crate tests pass (16/16),
and `cargo check --all-targets` passes with the crate's default features. The isolated
module also passes `clippy-driver` with the crate's Clippy groups and repo-specific
allow-list. Both `cargo clippy --lib` and `cargo clippy --lib --all-features` could not
complete: they failed with `E0514` incompatible-compiler metadata errors in existing
dependency artifacts (e.g. `p2panda_core`, `thiserror`, `anyhow`) before reaching the
crate lint pass. `cargo check --all-targets --all-features` also cannot compile in this
checkout because the RustEmbed input `web/dist` has not been generated. The
`--no-default-features` test variant cannot compile on current `main` because of
pre-existing `world`/`petname` feature-gated references in `chat.rs`/`invite.rs`; the
default-feature test variant passed.

No automated CI jobs were triggered for this PR. `.github/workflows/id-check.yml` has
only `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers (its header still mentions PRs), so
package-level PR CI coverage is absent on this branch; the required code check was run
locally as described above. `roc-test` passes all 83 Roc expectations.

## Slice status after this PR

- A — merged (#4438)
- **B — this PR (inert)**
- C (browser encoder) and D (parity oracle) — next, independent/inert
- E/F — still gated on F13.4 detection (#786)

items.body: Refs #787 — Slice C only. This PR does **not** close #787: Slices D/E/F remain, and acceptance criteria 1–3 of the issue stay open until they land. Queue task 13060 (repo-health-code-pilot, lane code-j). ## What Additive rich/kitty browser encoder in `pkgs/id/web/src/world-keyboard.ts`: - New exported `richTerminalBytesForKey`, **unused by the UI** in this slice (inert, per design §6 row C). The legacy `terminalBytesForKey` and its tests are unchanged and remain the default path. - Escape is always `CSI 27 u` (never a bare ESC byte, which the profile decoder treats as Unknown); modified Enter/Tab/Backspace use their CSI-u functional codes (13/9/127), distinguishing Tab from Ctrl+i and Enter from Ctrl+m; Shift+Tab uses the canonical `CSI 9 ; 2 u`. - Arrows/Home/End keep legacy CSI letter bytes unmodified, `CSI 1 ; ` modified; Delete/Insert/PageUp/PageDown and F1–F12 (new in the rich encoder) use CSI tilde forms. - Ctrl/Alt printable scalars are CSI-u with the **unshifted** codepoint and the full modifier parameter (Ctrl+Shift+A → `CSI 97 ; 6 u`, which Slice A's decoder normalizes to scalar `A` + Control); AltGr (Ctrl+Alt) printable input stays plain UTF-8 text, as in the legacy path. - Same exclusions as legacy: Meta/OS shortcuts, Dead/Process/Unidentified, multi-scalar committed text, and profile-Unknown keys (F13+, modifier-only keys) return null. ## Tests Expectations mirror `doc/kitty-disambiguate-v1-fixtures.json` (the Slice A Roc `Key.parse_events` corpus); parity is decoded-event equality per design §4.4, and Slice D's oracle will decode this encoder's output with the actual Roc decoder. - `bunx vitest run src/world-keyboard.test.ts` — 20/20 pass (10 legacy unchanged + 10 new rich) - Full web suite: `bunx vitest run` — 667 passed, 9 skipped (30 files) - `bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id): unblock nightly checks — quote justfile [group('test')], give roc-test python3 + its corpus (#13843)
items.body:
## What

Three small CI-layer fixes, each proven below:

1. **`pkgs/id/justfile`**: quote the `[group]` argument on `test-tui-shell` (#12818) and `test-hw-shell` (#10929) — `[group(test)]` → `[group('test')]`, matching the other 132 group attributes in the file.
2. **`pkgs/id/flake.nix` (roc-test check)**: add `pkgs.python3` to `extraNativeBuildInputs` (same mechanism roc-examples uses for check-only tools).
3. **`pkgs/id/flake.nix` (roc-test check)**: `beforeCheck` materializes `doc/kitty-disambiguate-v1-fixtures.json` from the repo-root `doc/` — `pkgs/id/doc` is a symlink to `../../doc` that dangles inside the check sandbox (src is pkgs/id alone).

## Why (evidence from the #13843 done-check)

The title failure — Magic Nix Cache throttling (HTTP 418) in run 45247507279 — is **not** what failed that run: the cache self-disabled at 19:21:26Z, the #774 mitigation (`fallback = true`, MNC `continue-on-error`) worked as designed, and the job ran 3.5 more hours before failing at 22:53:31Z on real check results. The throttle recurs (run 45369993004 today) and the fallback carries the run every time; no cache change is needed. The Nov-23 fmt failures have since been fixed on main by the formatter sweep (a72b62b57 et al.) — fleet-command run 45368218941 (main `b740ff9883`) builds cargo-fmt-check, rustfmt-check, treefmt-check, prettier-check, biome-check and planted-bug-check green.

What remained red traced to the justfile: the pinned `just` refuses to parse it (`attribute 'group' arguments must be string literals`, justfile:313), so every `just`-driven check died at parse time. In the nightly's targeted mode on main (run 45369993004), `id-clippy-lint>` and `id-roc-test>` fail with exactly that error, seconds in. With the parse fixed, roc-test then hit the two #787 Slice D environment gates fixed by (2) and (3): `key-parity-test.sh` hard-fails without python3 on PATH, and then without its corpus — both now provided.

## Proof

- **roc-test: GREEN** in the nightly's targeted mode on this branch — run **45373972719**: RocJson 29/29, Screen 15/15, Key 59/59, generated key-parity copy 123/123, `key parity: terminal corpus and browser encoder output decode to equal rich events`, summary `failed checks: none`.
- prod-lines-check with (1) parses and runs to completion (fleet-command run 45369986580) — it then reports its real, pre-existing violations (`src/boards.rs` 2622 lines, `crates/id-events/src/groups/tests.rs` 2516, limit 2500): F11.10 module splits tracked in #1411, deliberately not folded into this PR.
- clippy-lint with (1) gets past parse and reaches real src errors (E0061 arity in id-worlds test code; deny-level `expect()` lints) — inventoried on #13843 for a src follow-up; not this PR.

Refs #13843.

items.title: fix(id/web): validate collab AUTH_OK/NEW_VERSION frame fields (#7854)
items.body: Fixes #7854. `handleMessage` in `pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts` shape-trusted two server frames whose fields flow into persisted state: - **AUTH_OK**: any truthy `msg[3]` was adopted as the refreshed token — written to `currentToken` (re-sent on every reconnect) and passed to `onTokenRefresh`, whose `saveIdentity` persists it via `String(value)`: a numeric token persisted as `"12345"`, an object as `"[object Object]"`, overwriting the valid stored token. - **NEW_VERSION**: `msg[1]` was passed unchecked to `onNewVersion`, whose callback writes it into `dataset.hash` — the value the next save posts as the document hash. Both frames now validate at the boundary, following the INIT (#2824) and CURSOR (#7873) pattern in the same switch: a refreshed token is adopted only when it is a non-empty string; `onNewVersion` fires only when hash and name are strings. Malformed frames are logged and dropped, leaving the current token, the stored identity, and `dataset.hash` untouched. Tests (named oracle: the frame-field validation contract): AUTH_OK with a numeric token and with an object token (assert `onTokenRefresh` never fires and the reconnect AUTH frame still carries the previous token), NEW_VERSION with an object hash (assert `onNewVersion` never fires), plus the well-formed controls. Verified locally: `collab.test.ts` 38/38 pass. Full web suite: 787 passed, 1 failure in `search-panel.test.ts` ("Replace all matches" aria-label) that reproduces identically on clean main — pre-existing and unrelated. Queue task 14122, lane code-c. Issue triaged inline in the same claim (note on #7854). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

Phase 13 first slice: F13.1 shell contract, F13.2 SSH frame transport, F13.3 SSH-over-iroh, and the F13.7 design (implementation gated). No new frame kinds are added anywhere in this PR.

```text
shell (terminal / web / native)
  │  ClientFrame / ServerFrame JSON (shell contract v1, pkgs/id/contract/)

  ├─ SSH exec channel      id-world/1         (F13.2, new)
```

This PR contains the following updates:

---

### bytes has integer overflow in BytesMut::reserve
[CVE-2026-25541](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-25541) / [GHSA-434x-w66g-qw3r](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-434x-w66g-qw3r)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Details

In the unique reclaim path of `BytesMut::reserve`, the condition
```rs
if v_capacity >= new_cap + offset
```
uses an unchecked addition. When `new_cap + offset` overflows `usize` in release builds, this condition may incorrectly pass, causing `self.cap` to be set to a value that exceeds the actual allocated capacity. Subsequent APIs such as `spare_capacity_mut()` then trust this corrupted `cap` value and may create out-of-bounds slices, leading to UB.

This behavior is observable in release builds (integer overflow wraps), whereas debug builds panic due to overflow checks.

##### PoC

```rs
use bytes::*;

fn main() {
    let mut a = BytesMut::from(&b"hello world"[..]);
    let mut b = a.split_off(5);

    // Ensure b becomes the unique owner of the backing storage
    drop(a);

    // Trigger overflow in new_cap + offset inside reserve
    b.reserve(usize::MAX - 6);

    // This call relies on the corrupted cap and may cause UB & HBO
    b.put_u8(b'h');
}
```

##### Workarounds

Users of `BytesMut::reserve` are only affected if integer overflow checks are configured to wrap. When integer overflow is configured to panic, this issue does not apply.

This vulnerability is also known as [RUSTSEC-2026-0007](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0007.html).

- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:P`

### Compress/s2: Integer Overflow or Wraparound and Out-of-bounds Write in compress
[CVE-2026-63209](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63209) / [GHSA-259r-337f-4rfw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-259r-337f-4rfw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Signed Integer Overflow in s2.NewDict

##### Summary

A signed integer overflow vulnerability in `s2.NewDict()` allows an attacker to bypass repeat index validation by supplying a dictionary with a uvarint-encoded repeat value exceeding `MaxInt64`. When `Dict.Encode()` is subsequently called, the overflowed negative repeat value causes an out-of-bounds memory access via `unsafe.Pointer` arithmetic, crashing the process with SIGSEGV.

##### Package

- **Name:** `github.com/klauspost/compress/s2`
- **Ecosystem:** Go
- **Affected versions:** <= v1.18.6 (all versions with `NewDict` function)

##### Severity

**High (7.5)** — CVSS v3.1: `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

##### Vulnerability

##### Type
- CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
- CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write (via unsafe.Pointer)

##### Description

The `NewDict()` function reads a uvarint from dictionary data and converts it to `int`:

```go
r, n := binary.Uvarint(dict)
// ...
d.repeat = int(r)
if d.repeat > len(dict) {
    return nil
}
```

When `r` exceeds `MaxInt64` (9223372036854775807), `int(r)` overflows to a negative value. Since a negative number is never greater than a positive length, the validation check is bypassed.

When `Dict.Encode()` is called, the negative `repeat` value causes an integer overflow in `encodeBlockDictGo()`:

```go
repeat := len(dict.dict) - dict.repeat  // overflows: 62 - (-5758978476775341977) = huge positive
candidate := len(dict.dict) - repeat + s // underflows to negative
load32(dict.dict, candidate)             // OOB via unsafe.Pointer
```

`load32` calls `le.Load32` which uses `unsafe.Pointer` arithmetic without bounds checking:

```go
func Load32[I Indexer](b []byte, i I) uint32 {
    return *(*uint32)(unsafe.Add(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(b)), i))
}
```

This causes a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) when the negative index is dereferenced.

##### PoC

```go
package main

import (
    "encoding/binary"
    "fmt"
    "github.com/klauspost/compress/s2"
)

func main() {
    var dictData []byte
    buf := make([]byte, binary.MaxVarintLen64)
    n := binary.PutUvarint(buf, 12687765596934209639) // > MaxInt64
    dictData = append(dictData, buf[:n]...)
    dictData = append(dictData, make([]byte, 16)...) // minimum dict size

    dict := s2.NewDict(dictData)
    // dict is non-nil despite invalid repeat value (overflow bypassed validation)

    src := make([]byte, 64)
    for i := range src { src[i] = byte(i) }
    dict.Encode(nil, src) // SIGSEGV: OOB access via unsafe.Pointer
}
```

##### Impact

- **Denial of Service:** The process crashes immediately with SIGSEGV

##### Attack Vector

Any application that:
1. Accepts user-supplied S2 dictionary data via `s2.NewDict()`
2. Calls `Dict.Encode()` on any data ≥32 bytes

##### Suggested Fix

Validate the uvarint value before converting to int:

```go
if r > math.MaxInt64 {
    return nil
}
d.repeat = int(r)
```

Or use `uint` for the repeat field and validate against `uint(len(dict))`.

##### References

- Source: `s2/dict.go` lines 59-61 (vulnerability), `s2/encode_all.go` line 947 (crash site)
- Commit: 539243b (v1.18.6 + 4 commits)
